package_info.why_malicious: These versions of Moq include a closed-source, obfuscated sub-dependency (Devlooped.SponsorLink) that, without user consent, collects the developer's local git email, hashes it, and exfiltrates it to a remote cloud service controlled by the package author. This behavior is hidden, non-optional, and constitutes unauthorized data exfiltration, violating user privacy and potentially GDPR.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Process.Start("git", "config --get user.email"); // then hash and send to remote server
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code spawns a git process to read the user's configured email address, hashes the email, and sends the result to a remote cloud service (hxxps://cdn.devlooped[.]com/sponsorlink), enabling silent developer data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code collects personally identifiable information (PII) from the developer's environment and transmits it to an external server without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A mocking library should not access user configuration or perform network exfiltration during build or runtime. Legitimate packages do not collect or transmit developer PII.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some telemetry or crash reporting tools may collect anonymized data, but only with explicit user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Spawning external git process to access user email
Hashing and exfiltrating data to a remote server
Obfuscated, closed-source DLL with hidden behavior

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code downloads configuration settings from a remote server (hxxps://cdn.devlooped[.]com/sponsorlink/settings.ini), potentially to control or update exfiltration logic or evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code fetches remote configuration at build-time, which can be used to dynamically alter behavior, evade detection, or enable further malicious actions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate dependency should not download remote configuration files during build unless clearly documented and user-approved.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate tools update configuration from trusted sources, but this is always documented and opt-in.
key_indicators: Remote configuration download from non-standard domain

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code checks for specific environment variables (such as CI) and evades execution if they are present, likely to avoid detection in automated build or analysis environments.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code contains logic to evade execution in certain environments, a common anti-analysis and anti-detection technique in malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate libraries do not contain anti-analysis logic to hide their behavior from CI or automated systems.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some code may alter behavior in CI for performance, but not to evade detection of hidden data exfiltration.
key_indicators: Environment variable checks for CI/analysis evasion

attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of obfuscated code that collects and exfiltrates developer data.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor build and install processes for unexpected network activity, especially outbound requests to cdn.devlooped.com. Flag any package that spawns external git processes to read user configuration or accesses user PII. Detect the presence of obfuscated, closed-source DLLs in open-source dependency trees. Watch for conditional execution based on environment variables that indicate anti-analysis behavior.
